desk.why: Implied is only 0.84x the forecast, below the 1.10x a seller needs.

facts: NIFTY moved +5.6% over the last 7 sessions and +0.7% on the day, to 25,298.
Gap +62 pts, then the session added +86 pts.
The day closed in the upper half (close - low 97, high - close 45).
ATM IV sits in its 92nd percentile of the past year: option premium is rich - selling it pays more, but moves are expected to be bigger.

base.why: History says moves like this usually carry on (it reached 25,500 in 59.3% of past cases vs 56.1% normally), so the plan sells puts under the writers' floor at 25,000 and sells no call below 26,000. Note: the desk's volatility rule says stand aside today (Implied is only 0.84x the forecast, below the 1.10x a seller needs.). This plan overrides it only for the scenario branches; size down.
text: bull put spread: sell 25,000 PE, buy 24,800 PE (credit about 40 pts, Rs 2,577 per lot; max loss Rs 10,423)

scenarios.title: Drifts sideways between 25,000 and 25,500
watch: Two daily closes below 25,500 without a new high
Close - open (the body) small, either colour
scenarios.means: The move is pausing. Time decay is working for the seller.
scenarios.action: Hold. Add a bear call spread: sell 26,000 CE, buy 26,200 CE (credit about 14 pts, Rs 904 per lot; max loss Rs 12,096) to turn it into an iron condor.

scenarios.title: Reaches 25,500 and stalls
watch: High - close bigger than close - low (sellers took it back)
25,500 CE open interest still rising (call writers defending)
scenarios.means: Call writers are defending 25,500. A ceiling for now.
scenarios.action: Sell a bear call spread at 26,000 (sell 26,000 CE / buy 26,200 CE). Roll the put spread up to sell 25,200 PE / buy 24,900 PE to lock in what the rise earned.

scenarios.title: Breaks out above 25,500
watch: 25,500 CE open interest falling (writers buying back - short covering)
Close near the day's high again
scenarios.means: The ceiling gave way. Next magnets: 26,000 then 26,300.
scenarios.action: Do not sell calls at 26,000. Roll the put spread up to sell 25,700 PE / buy 25,400 PE. Sell calls only at 26,300 or above. If it spikes past 26,000 in one session with VIX rising, take profit instead of chasing.
scenarios.odds: Reached 26,000 in 20.0% and 26,300 in 10.0% of past cases (normal 16.0% / 7.9%).

scenarios.title: Pulls back to 25,000
watch: Holds: daily close above 25,000 and 25,000 PE open interest still rising
Breaks: daily close below 25,000 and 25,000 PE open interest falling
scenarios.means: A test of the put writers' floor. Shakeouts are normal after strong runs.
scenarios.action: If it holds: keep the position. If it breaks: exit the put spread (loss capped and known) and flip to a bear call spread, sell 25,300 CE / buy 25,500 CE. Next floors 24,800 then 24,300.
scenarios.odds: Dipped to 25,000 at some point in 35.7% of past cases (normal 38.8%).

rules: Take profit on any spread once 50% of its credit is earned; the rest is not worth the risk.
Close any spread once its loss reaches 1.5x the credit taken, whatever day that is. Holding into expiry is fine; size smaller on expiry day.
Act on daily closes, not intraday spikes. The OI checks use the next morning's bhavcopy.
Credits for rolls and add-ons are set by prices on the day you act; today's numbers are a guide only.
limits: None of the desk's positioning signals (PCR, max pain, OI flow, walls) has passed its own backtest for this horizon, so the history study is the main evidence.

horizons.label: Tomorrow (expiry day)
horizons.sizeNote: Half size: on expiry day premiums swing fast. Expiry-day shorts carry an extra 2% ELM (about Rs 32,887 per lot here) and get no calendar-spread offset; keep cash for it.
